variants.headline: Looking back: state payments fall short
variants.sub: The government has underpaid wages, unemployment benefit and pensions, each by an equal proportion.
variants.body:
We return to our earlier coverage. Our report recorded this: State wages, unemployment benefit and pensions have all been paid short by the same share.

A wage, benefit or pension is meant to support a life. Labour should not let an equal share of underpayment become a reason to forget that purpose. The arithmetic describes the cut; it does not replace the question of how people are expected to live with the payment they receive.

The event remains part of the record. Whether subsequent developments met the standard it raised is a separate question, not something the old headline can answer by itself.

The stewardship of {target} warrants examination against the unpaid portion. The uniform share describes how payments fell short; it does not by itself supply a verdict about responsibility for the position.

variants.headline: Looking back: equal cuts, different household needs
variants.sub: Government payments have fallen short across state wages, unemployment benefit and pensions alike.
variants.body:
